Jack Heart: "i tink iwant to see this go all the way to demo now, with decisions made by you / the worker until we're ready to demo it using some pufferlib thing". So: do not stop for open choices before the demo. Decide each remaining one yourself (RunAttempt writers, etude.job vs etude.jobs, cleanup with no controller, config on local --resume, second Ctrl-C, opener name, example names, anything new), record the choice and why in scratch/questions.md, and keep going. The demo is a small PufferLib environment trained with the new train API (track/run.save/stopping, stop and resume) and evaluated with the new eval API (author function returning a Benchmark, play(match) with a Pydantic match config). Keep pufferlib out of Etude's required dependencies and out of the network-denied test suite (an example project or optional extra); run it small and locally, no load. EXP-62 (PufferLib and Coworld examples) can build on whatever example lands here.
